claims.statement: For disjoint original-coordinate banks I,J with independent cap-one inputs, if Q=F(X_I)+2 X_I^T N X_J+b^T X_J, F arbitrary measurable, and sigma2(N)>0, then Q has a density and ||p_Q||infinity<=2sqrt(pi)/sigma2(N).
claims.mechanism: Condition on X_I; use the Ball/Rogozin one-dimensional linear-form density cap, project the coefficient to the top-two right singular plane, use the two-dimensional product projection density cap 2, then integrate the inverse radius by the bathtub principle.

This is not a QFORM counterexample; the new one-sided-curvature theorem bounds its full density by 2sqrt(pi).
On the live r49 global physical cut, e5(M^T M)>=1/1024 implies ||p_Q||infinity<=10sqrt(2e)<23.317.
